pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: The Delaware Journeyperson Electrician exam is administered by Prov, Inc. for licensing through the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation. The exam is computer-based, open book, and timed. The Delaware journeyperson electrician examination includes 70 questions and allows 3 hours of testing time. The passing score for Delaware electrician examinations is 75%. Exam results are provided after completion, and results are also reported to the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation. Candidates who need to retake the exam may do so after waiting at least seven days from the previous test attempt. The Delaware Journeyperson Electrician exam content outline includes general electrical theory and principles, plan reading, equipment for general use, motors and controls, wiring and protection, wiring methods and materials, communication systems, special conditions, special equipment, and special occupancies.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Wiring methods and materials is the largest listed content area, followed by wiring and protection and general electrical theory and principles, so candidates should build a study plan that gives enough attention to code application, installation rules, and electrical fundamentals. The exam tests the knowledge needed by a journey-level electrician working in the electrical trades while under the supervision of a Master Electrician. Candidates should prepare for questions that may require code lookup, rule interpretation, trade understanding, calculation skills, and familiarity with electrical installation terminology.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Delaware Journeyperson Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates may use approved reference books during testing, but all reference materials must follow the exam provider’s rules. The candidate information bulletin states that exams are open book and timed, and it also lists reference materials that may be used during testing. Reference-book preparation is important because open book does not mean the answers will be easy to find. Candidates need to know where common topics are located, how code articles are organized, how tables are used, and how to move through the NEC efficiently under timed conditions. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is intended to help candidates build that navigation skill during study. Prov’s reference material rules prohibit handwritten notes in reference books. Moveable tabs and Post-it notes are not permitted, photocopied reference books are not permitted, and test preparation study guides are not approved references in the testing center.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: Candidates may not highlight, underline, mark, or write information in reference materials during the exam. Permanent tabs and clean, approved references should be prepared before test day according to the exam provider’s rules. Because this product is based on the 2026 NEC, candidates should use the 2026 National Electrical Code during study sessions to build familiarity with the code cycle used for this preparation package. Code-navigation practice should include definitions, general requirements, wiring and protection, wiring methods, equipment rules, motors, special occupancies, special equipment, communication systems, and calculation-related tables.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Delaware journeyperson electrician licensing is handled through the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation’s DELPROS online system. Candidates may apply through different pathways, including examination, reciprocity, or certification, depending on their background and documentation. A candidate applying by examination must submit the required application materials through DELPROS and pass the journeyperson examination. Delaware also provides a certificate pathway for applicants who hold a certificate of completion issued by the Department of Labor or an approved apprenticeship program in Delaware, another state, a U.S. territory, or the District of Columbia. Reciprocity may be available for applicants who hold a current journeyperson license from another state, U.S. territory, or the District of Columbia, depending on the Board’s review of substantially similar licensing requirements and experience.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: A typical examination pathway includes creating or logging into a DELPROS account, selecting the correct journeyperson electrician application pathway, submitting the required application and fee, uploading or arranging required documentation, waiting for authorization or exam information, scheduling the exam through Prov, taking the Delaware Journeyperson Electrician exam, and completing any remaining licensing requirements through the Division of Professional Regulation.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Delaware requires individuals who perform electrical services in the state to hold the proper Delaware professional electrician license. The Board defines electrical services or electrical work as activity covered by the National Electrical Code as adopted by the Delaware State Fire Commission. A Delaware Journeyperson Electrician license allows the holder to perform electrical services under supervision while gaining additional experience and developing the skills needed for higher-level electrician license classifications. Delaware’s electrician license types include apprentice, residential, journeyperson, master, master special, limited, and limited special classifications. For examination applicants, Delaware requires Verification of Employment forms showing at least 8,000 hours of full-time experience performing electrical work under the supervision of a licensed master electrician, master electrician special, limited electrician, or limited electrician special.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: If a candidate cannot obtain an employment verification form for a period of employment, the state allows W-2 forms for those periods along with an explanation and detailed outline of experience. All journeyperson electrician applications are submitted through DELPROS. The Delaware system allows candidates to save an incomplete application and return to it later, but an application must be submitted within six months after it is started, or the candidate must restart the online application. Candidates should gather license verifications, employment forms, apprenticeship certificates when applicable, and other required documents before beginning the application process.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: The Delaware Journeyperson Electrician exam includes 70 questions over 3 hours. Candidates should practice working at a steady pace so they have enough time to read each question carefully, identify the subject area, locate the correct reference when needed, and answer without losing time in unnecessary code searches. The subject breakdown gives candidates a useful way to prioritize study time. Wiring methods and materials accounts for 22 questions, wiring and protection accounts for 14 questions, and general electrical theory and principles accounts for 9 questions. Other listed areas include plan reading, equipment for general use, motors and controls, communication systems, special conditions, special equipment, and special occupancies. The 2026 Delaware Journeyman Electrician Study Guide helps candidates organize their review around the skills and topics that matter for journeyperson electrician preparation. It supports trade-focused learning, code-based study, and practical review for candidates who need to connect field experience with test questions.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: The 2026 Electrician Calculations Study Guide is included because electrical math can be one of the most difficult parts of exam preparation. Candidates should practice formulas, unit conversions, conductor and load-related calculations, power relationships, voltage drop concepts, motor-related calculations, and other problem types that require careful step-by-step work. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs supports code-navigation practice. Candidates should use study time to learn the structure of the NEC, including definitions, chapter organization, article numbering, tables, exceptions, notes, and installation-specific requirements. Fast code navigation is especially important for open book exams because looking up every answer without a plan can use too much time. The 2026 Journeyman Electrician Flash Cards are useful for short study sessions and repeated review. Flash cards can help reinforce definitions, formulas, code terminology, safety concepts, and quick facts.

pieces.h: Test Information and Study Materials
pieces.t: Repetition is helpful for candidates who are balancing exam preparation with work, apprenticeship responsibilities, or family schedules. The 2026 Journeyman Electrician Exam Questions and Study Guide - Online Test Success Kit gives candidates practice with exam-style questions. Online practice can help identify weak areas, improve timing, and build familiarity with question formats. A strong study plan should combine reading, code lookup, calculations, flash card review, and online question practice instead of relying on only one type of study material.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Delaware electrical licensing is handled through the Delaware Division of Professional Regulation and the Delaware Board of Electrical Examiners. The Board must approve a candidate before the candidate may sit for the required examination. Delaware uses ProV as the external testing vendor for required electrical licensing examinations. The Delaware Master Electrician exam is a computer-based, open-book examination. The ProV candidate information bulletin lists the Delaware Master Electrician exam with 80 questions and 3 hours of testing time. The minimum passing score required by Delaware is 75%. The Delaware Master Electrician exam content outline includes General Electrical Knowledge, Plan Reading, Equipment for General Use, Wiring and Protection, Wiring Methods and Materials, Motors and Controls, Special Conditions, Special Equipment, Special Occupancies, and Communication Systems. These subject areas cover a broad range of electrical work, so candidates should build a balanced study plan instead of focusing only on one or two familiar topics.

pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Delaware defines a Master Electrician as a person licensed by the Board to plan, estimate, layout, perform, or supervise the installation, erection, or repair of electrical conductors, ducts, raceways, conduits, machinery, apparatus, devices, or fixtures for lighting, heating, or power in a structure. That scope makes the Master Electrician exam a broad trade examination that requires both code knowledge and practical electrical understanding. The Delaware Division of Professional Regulation states that all electrical examinations are based on the most up-to-date National Electrical Code adopted in Delaware. This product is based on the 2026 National Electrical Code for candidates preparing for the 2026 code cycle.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The Delaware Master Electrician exam is an open-book, timed exam. Candidates are allowed to use authorized references during testing, and those references are checked by the ProV test administrator before the candidate is permitted into the testing room. Open-book testing still requires strong preparation because candidates must know how to locate information quickly, apply rules correctly, and avoid wasting time searching through unfamiliar material. The ProV testing rules allow approved reference materials to be prepared with highlighting, underlining in pen only, and permanent tabs. Handwritten notes are not allowed in any portion of a reference book. Moveable tabs are not permitted, Post-it notes are not permitted, and photocopied documents cannot be added to a reference book. Candidates may bring a simple four-function calculator, but special calculators, tablets, phones, and similar devices are not permitted. The National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs included in this Ultimate Combo is a practical study tool for open-book exam preparation.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: Tabs help candidates organize their code book and practice moving through NEC articles, definitions, tables, wiring method rules, conductor requirements, overcurrent protection sections, grounding and bonding provisions, and special installation rules. Open book does not mean the answer will be obvious. Candidates still need to understand the question, identify the correct code topic, search efficiently, read exceptions carefully, and confirm the answer. A strong study routine should include repeated code-book practice, timed question sets, calculations review, and review of weak topics. The included study guides, flash cards, tabbed code book, and online exam questions work together to support that preparation process.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Delaware Master Electrician candidates begin by applying through DELPROS, the Delaware Professional Regulation Online Services portal. A candidate must create a DELPROS user account, begin the correct license application, submit the required application materials, and receive approval from the Board of Electrical Examiners before sitting for the examination. For examination applicants, Delaware requires proof of experience. For the Master Electrician license, Delaware lists six years of full-time experience under the supervision of a licensed Master Electrician, or four years of full-time experience under a Master Electrician plus an official transcript showing two years of technical training. Candidates who completed a registered or approved apprenticeship program may submit the required certificate of completion as part of the application process. Experience documentation is important. Delaware requires a Verification of Employment form from each employer when experience must be documented.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: For Delaware experience obtained after June 30, 2012, the candidate must have been licensed as an Apprentice Electrician or Journeyperson Electrician at the time for that experience to be credited. After the Board reviews and approves the application, the candidate receives notice of approval to sit for the exam. ProV then provides the examination registration information. Candidates schedule their exam through ProV and may test in person at available testing locations or through approved online testing when eligible. Candidates should follow all scheduling, identification, reference-material, and test-day rules listed by ProV. After passing the examination, Master Electrician applicants must submit proof of general liability insurance of at least $300,000. The applicant’s name must appear on the insurance document, even when coverage is provided through an employer’s policy. Once the Board office receives the passing score and confirms that the applicant has met all licensing requirements, the license may be issued.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Delaware requires a professional electrician license to perform electrical services in the state. Delaware defines electrical services or electrical work as activity covered by the National Electrical Code as adopted by the Delaware State Fire Commission. The Delaware Board of Electrical Examiners recognizes several license categories, including Master Electrician, Limited Electrician, Master Electrician Special, Limited Electrician Special, Journeyperson Electrician, Residential Electrician, and Apprentice Electrician. The Master Electrician license is the broad statewide license associated with planning, estimating, laying out, performing, or supervising electrical installation and repair work for lighting, heating, or power in structures. Candidates who do not qualify for the full Master Electrician license but have knowledge in a specialty area may apply for a Master Electrician Special license in approved specialty areas such as electric signs, elevators, HVAC, primary distribution systems, pools, or refrigeration.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Delaware also allows application by reciprocity for applicants who hold a current license of the same type from another state, United States territory, or the District of Columbia. Reciprocity requirements depend on whether the Board has determined that the other jurisdiction’s licensing standards are substantially similar to Delaware’s standards. Applicants applying by reciprocity may need to submit license verifications and, in some cases, proof of experience. Master and Limited Electrician applicants must provide proof of general liability insurance of at least $300,000 before the license can be issued. Applicants may take the exam before submitting proof of insurance, but the license cannot be issued until the Board receives acceptable proof. Electricians should also monitor renewal and continuing education requirements after licensure.
